decisions.summary: channel_end_on_stream judges a declaring channel end within half the stream's drawn width (the intake passes each stream's w, 7 ft fallback) instead of a flat 13 px
decisions.why: 0054 drawing: 'A meeting is a junction when either channel's end lies inside the other's drawn width'; half the width off the centerline is inside the width. Implementation moved to the research (FR-004). Aside: brook_rules.CROSSING_END_TOL = 13.0 ('meets it at a confluence') still judges the same thing at 13 px, and join_vertices' docstring still says rounding stays 'under the rule's 13' - both now stale against this fix.

decisions.summary: drawn_course holds a brook corner mitred where its rounding would carry the course more than w/2 off a confluence standing on that corner
decisions.why: 0054 drawing line 21: 'no watercourse on them has a mitered corner' (the GM's ruling of 2026-07-25: 'Water turns on a SWEPT BEND, never a mitred corner'); line 24 exempts only an offtake where 'the main channel is not turning there'; the code's own course_corner docstring says holding such a vertex 'would leave the bend mitred, which the brook's rounding exists to forbid'. The hold satisfies one 0054 rule by carving a case out of another - an 'except where' the GM's request ('I'm not sure there's any reason for our implementation to not match for anything') does not admit. It is not physically necessary: the confluence can be kept off corners (sink.brook_join already does so for the drain), or the channel's mouth moved onto the rounded course, either of which meets both rules. That no pool map moves today does not make the carve-out faithful; it means it can be removed at no map cost.

decisions.summary: cluster.py::belt_off_canvas#belt distance upwind (NEEDS-RESEARCH) tiered E0: depth re-cited to 0071 drawing's 80-120 ft convention, the 36 ft near face labeled UNRESEARCHED
decisions.why: A NEEDS-RESEARCH row normally goes E4 (spec Edge Cases). Here the function only samples belt_polygon's own band; its 36 ft is BELT_NEAR_FT, already claimed 'near stand-off - UNRESEARCHED' at its constant (hinterland/belt.py:114-115), and its 100 ft depth is BELT_DEPTH_FT, already cited to 0071 drawing line 12 (unedited since feature 329's rename). The new claim restates what the record and the source constant already say; a research pass would be research for an openly UNRESEARCHED constant, which the accepted spec puts outside the feature (Decisions: the 727 UNRESEARCHED claims are out of scope). Nothing the code does changes.

decisions.summary: plan.py::BELT_REACH#belt's far row (NEEDS-RESEARCH) tiered E0 and re-cited the same way: 0071's drawn depth, the near face UNRESEARCHED, the 10 ft rag
decisions.why: Same ground as W41-3, judged separately: 146 = BELT_NEAR_FT 36 (already UNRESEARCHED at its constant) + BELT_DEPTH_FT 100 (already cited to 0071 drawing) + BELT_FAR_RAG_FT 10 (already cited to 0071 drawing). The old citation of 0072 named a figure 0072 does not hold; the new claim points at where each part already stands. Value unchanged.
